displayName: Diagnostic Coronary Angiography — right femoral access
briefing: 62-year-old with exertional chest pain and a positive stress test. Right femoral access. Assess both coronary systems, then close. Keep screening time, contrast and dose to a minimum.

steps.title: Arterial access
steps.instruction: Puncture the right common femoral artery and place the sheath. Advance the needle smoothly — excessive force provokes a vagal response.
steps.hint: Aim below the inguinal ligament and over the femoral head.

steps.title: Advance to the aortic root
steps.instruction: Track the catheter up the iliac and aorta, over the arch, into the root.
steps.hint: The arch is the tortuous part — advance in short pushes rather than one long one.

steps.title: Set the LAO cranial projection
steps.instruction: Angulate the C-arm to LAO 40 / cranial 20 before engaging the left system.

steps.title: Engage the left main
steps.instruction: Torque the catheter to the left coronary cusp and engage the left main ostium.
steps.hint: Rotate counter-clockwise from neutral. Do not sit in the ostium longer than you need — damping causes ischaemia.

steps.title: Image the left system
steps.instruction: Inject contrast and record the left coronary run.
steps.hint: A short, firm injection opacifies better than a long weak one, and costs less contrast.

steps.title: Engage the right coronary
steps.instruction: Disengage, reposition to the right coronary cusp and engage the RCA.
steps.hint: Clockwise torque from neutral, slightly higher in the root than the left main.

steps.title: Image the right system
steps.instruction: Inject contrast and record the right coronary run.

steps.title: Withdraw the catheter
steps.instruction: Disengage and withdraw the catheter back to the access site.

steps.title: Haemostasis
steps.instruction: Remove the sheath and achieve haemostasis at the access site.
steps.hint: Hold above the arteriotomy, not on the skin puncture.
